Seek relevant scientific papers for all critical adjustments on ones own theory. These theories must be meet SOFT_PROVEN [SP] standards. SPINALTAP_ALGORITHM "A series of modular algorithms designed by treating the human nervous system as a framework ideology for a mathematic 3D engine. To collapse all relationships, the mathematic sequence simplified is nervous_system[1] -> vertebrae[2] -> spinal_column[3]"

nervous_system "large algorithm batch with a narrow scope of work. Each sequence comples their own set of formulations to cohesively run one ecosystem. They all have their own different, unique purposes that operate the ecosystem that is interdependant. The most simple and modular modules. Covers vastly more things but do not over extend their complexity from each modulated area of the nervous_system."
vertebrae "The smaller modular algorithm formulations designed to operate correlated data delivered from its data ingestion target or delivery point."
spinal_column "The algorithm that ingests/formulates all of the data from vertebrae and nervous_sytem."
CONTEXT_WEIGHT "The weight in which you utilize the discovered data into completing the task or request output/solution."
DO_NOT "Used to indicate when an item needs to be ignored or released from contextual relevance."

DONOT01 "DATA_REPLICATION: DO_NOT over estimate context weight into established original theories, this often leads to slight changes of the originals and often replicated outcomes or entirely the same."

ALGORITHMIC_STEM "Used to descrive the general theory of operation to utilize smaller batch algorithm "stems" that formulate their scoped jobs, and feed that data to a larger parent batch of "stems" designed to ingest their data and complete their own formulative scope."

CORE_THEORY "The fundamental idea or framework describing how the theory operates, what problem it solves, and how the algorithmic engine model is organized."
TECHNICALLY_PLAUSIBLE "A creative theory standard that permits novelty and exploratory mathematical structure while rejecting incoherent, unbounded, or non-actionable speculation."

SOFT_PROVEN "A research-supported plausibility standard. A theory is soft-proven when it has coherent mathematics, explicit assumptions, research comparison, critical adjustment, and enough internal consistency to proceed without live engine test data."
WORKFLOW "The ordered roadmap of the project from theory generation to research, proposal, docspec, and sourcecode development."

THEORY_CANDIDATE "A brainstormed or research-adjusted theoretical object that may become part of the SPINALTAP_ALGORITHM engine model."
SIGNAL_ROUTING_SPINE "A candidate theory where independent module outputs are converted into typed state signals before being aggregated through spinal_column [SA03]."
VERTEBRAE_LOCAL_SOLVERS "A candidate theory where small scoped solver units [SA02] perform specific transformations, collisions, corrections, style constraints, or state changes."
CONTEXT_WEIGHT_GOVERNOR "A candidate theory for measuring, limiting, and documenting how strongly outside research can influence the internal theory [CW], [DN01]."
STYLE_CONSTRAINT_LAYER "A candidate theory where visual style is treated as a formal constraint surface that can shape rendering, asset rules, and engine presentation [SY]."
SOFT_PROOF_PIPELINE "A candidate theory for moving an idea from raw brainstorm to TECHNICALLY_PLAUSIBLE [TP], then toward SOFT_PROVEN [SP]."

SPINALTAP_ALGORITHM "A series of modular algorithms organized through a nervous-system-inspired framework for a mathematical 3D engine. The simplified structure is nervous_system [SA01] -> vertebrae [SA02] -> spinal_column [SA03]."

nervous_system "A broad but bounded algorithm family. Each nervous_system domain contains multiple scoped formulations and contributes to the overall engine ecosystem without owning the entire system."
vertebrae "A smaller modular algorithm, local solver, transform unit, or scoped formulation that operates on a defined data target, module boundary, or delivery point."
spinal_column "The aggregation, routing, and reconciliation layer that ingests outputs from vertebrae and nervous_system modules, orders their relationships, and produces higher-order engine state."

ALGORITHMIC_STEM "A modular theory of operation where smaller scoped algorithmic stems formulate their assigned jobs and feed bounded results into larger parent stems that ingest, reconcile, and continue the formulation chain."

CONTEXT_WEIGHT "The amount of influence discovered data, source material, research, or prior theory is allowed to have on the current output. High context weight requires stronger anti-replication discipline."
DO_NOT "A negative constraint used to remove, ignore, limit, or release an item from contextual relevance."

DATA_REPLICATION "Do not over-weight established theories so heavily that the result becomes a lightly modified replica of the original. Extract constraints, failures, and useful principles without recreating the source."
STYLE "A formal video-game design or rendering style marker, usually framed around computational platform capability, rendering behavior, or visual presentation constraints."
LOW_POLY_3D "A reduced-polygon 3D modeling style where simplified geometry is an intentional visual and computational feature."
TEXTURE_MAPPED_LOW_POLY_3D "A low-poly 3D style where image textures provide most surface detail over simplified geometry."
AFFINE_TEXTURED_3D "A retro 3D texture-mapping style associated with perspective-imperfect or visibly warped texture behavior."
DITHERED_3D "A visual style using dithering, color limitation, or noise-pattern transitions to create retro shading and color behavior."
VERTEX_LIT_3D "A lighting style where illumination is calculated at vertices and interpolated across polygon faces."
GOURAUD_SHADED_3D "A smooth polygonal shading style based on interpolated vertex color or lighting values."
FLAT_SHADED_3D "A hard-faceted 3D style where individual polygon planes remain visually distinct."
BILLBOARDED_3D "A 3D presentation technique where 2D planes or sprites are placed and oriented within a 3D scene."
PRE_RENDERED_3D "A presentation style using offline-rendered 3D backgrounds, sprites, or assets inside a real-time or interactive context."
FIXED_FUNCTION_3D "A 3D rendering style associated with pre-modern-shader hardware behavior and limited programmable graphics control."
CEL_SHADED_TOON_SHADED_3D "A stylized 3D rendering approach using simplified lighting, color ramps, outlines, or cartoon-like presentation."
ARCADE_3D "A clean, bright, readable real-time 3D aesthetic associated with arcade 3D presentation."
EARLY_REAL_TIME_CGI "A glossy or toy-like 3D presentation style that imitates early offline CGI while remaining real-time."
SIXTH_GENERATION_3D "A 3D style language associated with Dreamcast, PlayStation 2, GameCube, and original Xbox-era presentation."
RETRO_3D "A broad modern umbrella style for recreating, remixing, or constraining older real-time 3D aesthetics."
IGNORE "A contextual ignore marker used to remove a style, concept, source, or direction from active design relevance."
STYLE "Ignore traditional pixel_art as an engine-level or core-design solution for this document."

RESEARCH_SOURCE "A real external source entry such as a paper, book, article, documentation page, talk, or implementation note. A complete source record should include title, source, year, link or DOI when available, usage context, context weight, and linked pseudo-citation markers."
OPEN_RESEARCH_SOURCE_SLOT "Reserved draft-only research-source placeholder. Use while a source is being identified, then replace with a complete numbered source record."
UNIQUE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH "Every active marker should have exactly one source-of-truth definition in [Z]."
SHARED_METADATA_SYNTAX "Blockquote metadata should use the same marker, category, and quoted-definition syntax as registry entries."

SAFE_QUOTATION_RULE "Definitions should avoid unescaped nested double quotes; use apostrophes inside definition strings when needed."
EXTERNAL_CLAIM_LINKAGE "External factual or research claims should be connected to a research-source record [RS]."
